candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: collaborate with public-health and interprofessional resources, follow reporting systems, and contribute to coordinated responses during emergencies and communicable-disease events.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — public-health coordination for cross-border infectious threats
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize global health security as coordinated cross-border preparedness, detection, reporting, and response under the International Health Regulations rather than isolated national action or unilateral WHO control of domestic health measures.

options.A: Cross-border health threats require countries to maintain capacities to detect, report, and respond to significant public-health events and to coordinate when international spread is possible.
options.B: Countries should manage infectious threats independently because sharing surveillance information across borders is outside current international health frameworks.
options.C: International health-security systems apply only after a pandemic has been declared and have no role in earlier outbreak detection or reporting.
options.D: WHO can unilaterally impose any clinical or public-health measure inside a country once an international event is reported.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The International Health Regulations (IHR), as amended in 2024 and in force for most States Parties since September 19, 2025, provide the global framework for preventing, preparing for, detecting, reporting, and responding to public-health threats that can cross borders. B and C contradict the IHR emphasis on surveillance, notification, preparedness, and coordinated response before and during international emergencies. D is incorrect because WHO serves a coordinating and technical role under the IHR and does not have authority to force health measures on countries or populations.
candidate.source_claim_supported: The current IHR support national capacities and international coordination for preparedness, detection, reporting, and response to public-health threats with cross-border implications while preserving national authority over domestic health measures.
candidate.source_document_title: International Health Regulations (2005), as amended in 2014, 2022 and 2024; Amended International Health Regulations Enter into Force
candidate.source_locator: WHO International Health Regulations topic page — current amended IHR text and functions supporting surveillance, assessment, information sharing, technical assistance, and emergency coordination. WHO Q&A on amendments — WHO cannot force lockdowns or other health measures on a country's population.

candidate.stem: A nurse caring for travelers during an unusual infectious-disease event is told that local findings may contribute to an international public-health response. Which statement best describes the health-security principle involved?
